root_cause.text: The `rose_kill_by_device()` function in the ROSE network protocol incorrectly uses the total count variable `cnt` instead of the loop iterator variable `i` to index the socket array during iteration.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff in `net/rose/af_rose.c` shows that inside the loop `for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++)`, the statement `sk = array[cnt];` was corrected to `sk = array[i];`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix out-of-bounds array access in rose_kill_by_device by using the correct loop iterator variable.
intent_record.what: The array index used to retrieve the socket pointer inside the loop was changed from the constant 'cnt' to the loop iterator variable 'i'.
intent_record.how: This prevents an out-of-bounds memory access and ensures that the function correctly iterates over and processes every socket in the array instead of repeatedly accessing an invalid index.
